newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: China data confirms large diesel imports - traders.
newsitem.headline: China data confirms large diesel imports - traders.

text.p: Customs data from China has confirmed that diesel imports surged in early 1997 in response to a loosening of import policies, traders said on Tuesday.
The customs data showed China imported a large 817,737 tonnes of light diesel in February, adding to imports in January of 451,775 tonnes.
The February imports meant that combined January/February imports at 1.27 million tonnes were 97 percent higher than the same period in 1996.
The surge in imports reflected China's move late in 1996 to encourage a surge in imports to counter sharply falling stocks, market sources said.
International diesel prices rose to five-year highs late in 1996, prompting China to use up stocks, instead of buying expensive imports.
Oil industry officials said late in December that one million tonnes of imports were needed urgently to overcome a growing domestic shortage.
China normally imports just under 400,000 tonnes of diesel each month. Imports in 1996 were around 4.5 million tonnes.

However, the surge in imports may have left inland stockpiles too high. Chinese oil sources now say state trader Sinopec has appealed to Beijing to slow down imports in the second quarter because of a glut inland.
"Refiners are not making any money at all because of the import glut," one refiner said.
In addition, retail prices have fallen below state-set ex-refinery prices in some regions, the sources said.
One refiner said that in the region of Shenzhen, on the south coast, retail prices were 2,130-2,150 yuan per tonne, when the wholesale price was 2,190 yuan.
